ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.claim: Favours and deprivation test whether people become grateful and fulfill others' rights or grow conceited, and whether they remain content or despair; the peaceful soul succeeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.anchor: He is testing whether blessing someone with favours makes him grateful

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.claim: The successful are content with God's will through prosperity and hardship, fulfilling others' rights when favoured and remaining patient when tried.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.anchor: they showed patience and resolve and expressed contentment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p315/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p315/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p315/r2.claim: Having succeeded in their trial and become worthy of Paradise, the contented souls are invited to join God's servants close to Him and enter Paradise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p315/r2.anchor: since they have become worthy of Paradise after succeeding in their trial, they should now join His near ones in Paradise.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes the soul as spirit and “enter among My servants” as entering the servants' bodies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: النفس والروح، والمعنى: فادخلي في أجساد عبادي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد وأبو جعفر وأبو صالح والكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r6.claim: Most readers use the plural “My servants”; these authorities read the singular “My servant.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: في عبادي جمعا وابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r7.claim: The singular can be a generic noun with the same denotation as the plural; alternatively it means entering the servant's body.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r7.anchor: والأظهر أنه أريد به اسم الجنس، فمدلوله ومدلول الجمع واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r9.claim: The verse has also been specifically associated with ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan, Hamza, or Khubayb ibn ʿAdi.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r9.anchor: قيل: في عثمان بن عفان. وقيل: في حمزة. وقيل: في خبيب بن عدي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r8.claim: Entering among God's servants means joining their company, followed by entering Paradise.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r19.speaker: أبي بن كعب
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r19.claim: Ubayy's reading has the singular: enter among my servant.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r19.anchor: في حرف أبي بن كعب : فادخلي في عبدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r20.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r20.claim: Entering among God's servants may mean entering into obedience to Him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r21.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r21.claim: It may mean entering with God's servants.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r21.anchor: الثالث : معناه فادخلي مع عبادي , قاله السدي .

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.claim: Later additions in 23–24 and 27–30 bring the afterlife dimension into the sura and help decode the enigmatic oath.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.anchor: Spätere Zusätze (V. 23.24 und V. 27–30) tragen diese eschatologische Dimension dann auch in die vorliegende Sure ein

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.claim: Verses 23–24 and 27–30 are later insertions that expand the original four-verse eschatological unit and enact the oath's duality as an antithesis.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.anchor: V. 23.24 sind wie V. 27–30 spätere Einschübe (s. o.), die das eschatologische Vierergesätz

THALABI:v10p203#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
THALABI:v10p203#2/r1.claim: The believer rests in a spacious grave, lit by Quran or a sunlike light, like a bride asleep until a loved one wakes her; the unbeliever is sent a foul, coarse covering and told to depart to torment.
THALABI:v10p203#2/r1.anchor: ثم يؤمر فيوسع عليه قبره سبعون ذراعا عرضه وسبعون ذراعا طوله وينبت له فيه الريحان

THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.claim: At Ibn Abbas's burial, a bird entered his coffin and was not seen leaving; the verse was recited at the grave, though its reciter was unseen.
THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: مات ابن عباس بالطائف فجاء طائر لم ير على خلقه

THALABI:v10p204/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p204/r4.speaker: مقاتل والقرظي وأبو عبيدة
THALABI:v10p204/r4.claim: They take 'enter among My servants' and 'enter My garden' as an inverted sequence meaning enter Paradise with God's servants.
THALABI:v10p204/r4.anchor: فادخلي في عبادي قال بعضهم: يعني مع عبادي جنتي في معنى الآية تقديم وتأخير

THALABI:v10p204/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p204/r5.speaker: الأخفش
THALABI:v10p204/r5.claim: He interprets 'among My servants' as belonging to God's party.

QASHANI:89:27-30/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:89:27-30/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:89:27-30/r3.claim: Entering God’s servants means joining His special servants who have realized essential unity.
QASHANI:89:27-30/r3.anchor: في زمرة عبادي المخصوصين بي من أهل التوحيد الذاتي

QASHANI:89:27-30/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:89:27-30/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:89:27-30/r5.claim: Two variant readings are reported: in My servant, and in the body of My servant; the latter refers to resurrection and the return of spirits to bodies.
QASHANI:89:27-30/r5.anchor: وقرىء في عبدي وقرىء في جسد عبدي أي: حالة البعث والنشور

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the soul is pleased by its promised reward and approved through its deeds; entering among God's servants means entering among the believers.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : ارجعي إلى ربك راضية قال : بما اعطيت من الثواب مرضية عنها بعلمها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says that when God takes a believer, the soul and God are mutually pleased; He then takes it into Paradise among His righteous servants.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله : يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة الاية قال : ان الله اذا اراد قبض عبده المؤمن اطمانت النفس اليه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r1.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r1.claim: Abu Salih says return to God is the soul's departure from the world at death; on Resurrection it is told to enter among God's servants and into Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r1.anchor: عن أبي صالح رضي الله عنه في قوله : ارجعي إلى ربك قال : هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r2.claim: Qatada says the tranquil soul is a believer reassured by God's promise and that entering among His servants means joining the righteous.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r2.anchor: عن قتادة يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة قال : هذا المؤمن اطمان إلى ما وعد الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r3.claim: Al-Suddi glosses entering among God's servants as entering with them.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r3.anchor: عن السدى رضي الله عنه فادخلي في عبادي قال مع عبادي

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the soul receives the good news of Paradise at death, resurrection, and the gathering.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم رضي الله عنه يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة الاية قال : بشرت بالجنة عند الموت وعند البعث ويوم الجمع

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr recounts that after Ibn Abbas died at Taif, an unseen bird entered his bier and did not emerge; the tranquil-soul verses were heard recited at his grave.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال : مات ابن عباس بالطائف ، فجاء طير لم ير على خلقه ، فدخل نعشه ثم لم ير خارجا منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.claim: The passage ends the warnings with glad tidings for believers guided by the Quran, following the Quran's pattern of joining promise to warning to encourage good and deter evil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.anchor: ختم الكلام بالبشارة للمؤمنين الذين تذكروا بالقرآن واتبعوا هديه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r4.claim: Because these verses follow the preceding passage in recitation and the codex, their original sequence likely reflects one revelation; the address is then spoken in the afterlife as an answer to the earth's crushing, with the intervening material parenthetical.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r4.anchor: فهذا قول يصدر يوم القيامة من جانب القدس من كلام الله تعالى أو من كلام الملائكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r5.claim: If God speaks, rabbiki replaces an implicit pronoun and expresses closeness and honor; if angels speak, it is ordinary wording, and God takes up their address by commanding the soul to enter among His servants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r5.anchor: فإن كان من كلام الله تعالى كان قوله : { إلى ربك } إظهارا في مقام الإضمار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r1.claim: Alternatively, the address may begin a new passage, prompted by the mention of punishment for the polytheist, and God may be speaking directly to the believers' reassured souls.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الآية استئنافا ابتدائيا جرى على مناسبة ذكر عذاب الإنسان المشرك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r3.claim: The first-person suffixes in My servants and My Paradise shift from the preceding third-person address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r3.anchor: والإضمار في قوله : { في عبادي } وقوله : { جنتي } التفات من الغيبة إلى التكلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r4.claim: Entering among God's servants and His Paradise details the general glad tiding, repeating the joy of the promised soul.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r4.anchor: فهو تفصيل بعد الإجمال لتكرير إدخال السرور على أهلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r5.claim: The servants are the righteous, inferred from the honored possessive construction and its pairing with Paradise; the phrase resembles God's promise in another verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r5.anchor: والمراد العباد الصالحون بقرينة مقام الإضافة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r6.claim: Being among them expresses actual inclusion and, by implication, companionship with the prophets and other blessed people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r6.anchor: فالظرفية حقيقية وتؤول إلى معنى المعية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r9.claim: Repeating the command to enter, rather than using one command with both objects, emphasizes Paradise itself and secures the hearers' joy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r9.anchor: فلم يقل : فادخلي جنتي في عبادي للاهتمام بالدخول

TUSTARI:89:29/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:89:29/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:89:29/r1.claim: Entering among God's servants means joining His friends, who are truly His servants.
TUSTARI:89:29/r1.anchor: أي في جملة أوليائي الذين هم عبادي حقا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r5.claim: On the death interpretation, “among My servants” means among the number of God's righteous servants; the common reading has the plural “My servants.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r5.anchor:
وقوله في عبادي أي في أعداد عبادي الصالحين، وهذه قراءة الجمهور
بجمع «عبادي»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r7.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r7.claim: Some say the address is for believers now, urging them to persevere until they return content and accepted; nafs here is generic.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r7.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: هذا النداء هو الآن للمؤمنين لما ذكر حال الكفار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وأبو شيخ والضحاك واليماني ومجاهد وأبو جعفر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r8.claim: They read “enter into My servant” in the singular, addressing an individual soul rather than a generic class.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعكرمة وأبو شيخ والضحاك واليماني ومجاهد وأبو جعفر: «فادخلي في عبدي»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r9.speaker: أبو شيخ
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r9.claim: Abu Shaykh explains the singular reading as the spirit entering the body.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r9.anchor: قال أبو شيخ: الروح يدخل في البدن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r11.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r11.claim: Salim ibn Abd Allah reads “enter among My servants and enter My garden.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r11.anchor: وقرأ سالم بن عبد الله «فادخلي في عبادي ولجي جنتي»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r12.claim: The singular “My servant” can be a collective expression uniting God's servants, like the prophetic saying that they are one hand against outsiders.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p481/r12.anchor: وتحتمل قراءة «عبدي» أن يكون العبد اسم جنس جعل عباده كالشيء الواحد دلالة على الالتحام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r1.claim: The soul is commanded to join God's chosen servants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r1.anchor: أي في جملة عبادي المصطفين قال أبو صالح يقال لها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r2.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says “return to your Lord” is said at death, while “enter among My servants” is said at resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو صالح يقال لها عند الموت ارجعي إلى ربك فإذا كان يوم القيامة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the phrase as entering together with God's servants.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r4.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص وأبي بن كعب وابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك وأبو العالية وأبو عمران
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r4.claim: These readers use the singular “My servant” instead of plural “My servants.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ سعد بن أبي وقاص وأبي بن كعب وابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك وأبو العالية وأبو عمران في عبدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj says that with the singular reading, “return to your Lord” means return to the person whose body the soul left and enter into him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124#2/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج فعلى هذه القراءة والله أعلم يكون المعنى ارجعي الي ربك أي إلى صاحبك الذي خرجت منه

FARRA:v3p262/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p262/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v3p262/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās alone reads “enter among My servant” and “enter My Garden” in the singular; the common reading has “My servants.”
FARRA:v3p262/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وحده: «فادخلي في عبدي ، وادخلي جنتي» والعوام (في عبادي)

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r5.claim: Entering among God's servants means joining the righteous servants and their ranks, then entering Paradise with them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r5.anchor: في جملة عبادي الصالحين ، وانتظمي في سلكهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r6.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r6.claim: An alternative takes the soul to mean the spirit and the command to enter among God's servants to mean entering their bodies.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : النفس الروح . ومعناه : فادخلي في أجساد عبادي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the phrase as entering into God's singular servant.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس : ( فادخلي في عبدي )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r8.claim: Ibn Masud reads the phrase as entering into God's servant's body.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : ( في جسد عبدي )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r9.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r9.claim: Ubayy reads the address as coming to the Lord content and approved, then entering into God's servant.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبي : ( ائتي ربك راضية مرضية ، ادخلي في عبدي )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r11.claim: A report promises forgiveness for reciting al-Fajr during the ten nights and light on Judgment Day for reciting it at other times.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r11.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1301 ) ( من قرأ سورة الفجر

MUQATIL:89:27-30/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r3.claim: Entering among God's servants means entering His mercy, and entering the Garden is entering it through that mercy.
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r3.anchor: يعني في رحمتى { وادخلي } من رحمتي في { جنتي }

MUQATIL:89:27-30/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r4.claim: The wording parallels Solomon's prayer to be admitted by mercy among God's righteous servants.
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r4.anchor: نظيرها في طس النمل، قول سليمان بن داود، عليهما السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#3/r1.claim: The soul joins the company of God's righteous servants and enters their ranks.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#3/r1.anchor: فى جملة عبادى الصالحين فانتظمى فى سلكهم

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r9.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r9.claim: “Enter among My servants” means enter their bodies, as the variant readings indicate; Ibn Abbas places this at resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r9.anchor: { فادخلي في عبادي } أي في أجساد عبادي دليله قراءة ابن عباس وابن مسعود

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r10.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak likewise places entry among God’s servants at resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذا يوم القيامة وقاله الضحاك

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r12.claim: “Among My servants” means among the righteous, linked to 29:9.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r12.anchor: ومعنى «في عبادي» أي في الصالحين من عبادي كما قال

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r13.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r13.claim: Al-Akhfash takes “among My servants” to mean “among My party”; the meaning is joining their company.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r13.anchor: وقال الأخفش: { في عبادي } أي في حزبي والمعنى واحد

NAHHAS:v5p225/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p225/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p225/r6.claim: Entering among God's servants means joining the righteous and being with them.
NAHHAS:v5p225/r6.anchor: أي في عبادي الصالحين أي كوني معهم

NAHHAS:v5p225/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p225/r7.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p225/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Ibn ʿAbbās alone read fī ʿabdī in the singular.
NAHHAS:v5p225/r7.anchor: قال الفراء وقرأ ابن عباس وحده ( فادخلي في عبدي )

NAHHAS:v5p225/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p225/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p225/r8.claim: The author rejects calling it Ibn ʿAbbās's unique reading: Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Abū Jaʿfar, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk also read it.
NAHHAS:v5p225/r8.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وهذا غلط أعني قوله وحده هذه قراءة مجاهد وعكرمة وأبي جعفر والضحاك

NAHHAS:v5p225/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p225/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p225/r9.claim: The singular may be generic, meaning each soul enters a servant, or one may stand for a collective.
NAHHAS:v5p225/r9.anchor: وتقديرها في العربية على معنى الجنس أي لتدخل كل روح في عبد وقيل هو واحد يدل على جمع

NAHHAS:v5p225/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p225/r10.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v5p225/r10.claim: The Kufans call deletion of the nūn in adkhulī a jussive marker.
NAHHAS:v5p225/r10.anchor: وعلامة الجزم في ادخلي عند الكوفيين حذف النون

NAHHAS:v5p225/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p225/r11.speaker: البصريون
NAHHAS:v5p225/r11.claim: The Basrans say the imperative is not inflected because it is neither an imperfect verb nor governed by a jussive particle.
NAHHAS:v5p225/r11.anchor: والبصريون يقولون ليس بمعرب لأنه غير مضارع ولا عامل معه فيجزمه

NAHHAS:v5p225/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p225/r12.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p225/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says an omitted lām is the governing particle.
NAHHAS:v5p225/r12.anchor: وزعم الفراء أن العامل فيه اللام وهي محذوفة

QUTB-ZILAL:89:29/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:29/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:29/r1.claim: Entering among God's servants means joining the chosen, brought near to attain this intimacy.

RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r3.claim: If it occurs at resurrection, “return” means returning to God's reward and re-entering the body from which the soul departed.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r3.anchor: أنه إنما يوجد عند البعث والقيامة ، والمعنى : ارجعي إلى ثواب ربك ، فادخلي في عبادي

RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r1.claim: One occasion-of-revelation report connects the verse to Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r1.anchor: قيل : نزلت في حمزة بن عبد المطلب

RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r2.claim: Another report connects it to Khubayb ibn ʿAdī, crucified by Meccans facing Medina; his prayer to face the sacred city was granted.
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r2.anchor: وقيل : في خبيت بن عدي الذي صلبه أهل مكة ، وجعلوا وجهه إلى المدينة

RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r3.claim: Razi stresses that the wording's general meaning governs beyond the specific reported occasion.
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r3.anchor: وأنت قد عرفت أن العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب

RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r4.claim: Entering among God's servants means joining His close servants and is a noble spiritual state.
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r4.anchor: ادخلى * فى عبادى } أي انضمي إلى عبادي المقربين ، وهذه حالة شريفة

RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r5.claim: Razi compares purified souls to polished mirrors: joined together, they reflect one another and increase spiritual joy and rank.
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r5.anchor: فإذا انضم بعضها إلى البعض حصلت فيما بينها حالة شبيهة بالحالة الحاصلة عند تقابل المرايا المصقولة

RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r6.claim: He links this spiritual state with the greeting to the companions of the right in 56:90–91.
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r6.anchor: وهذا هو المراد من قوله تعالى : { وأما إن كان من أصحاب اليمين * فسلام لك من أصحاب اليمين

RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r8.claim: The spiritual garden follows immediately at death, which Razi associates with the particle fa in “enter among My servants.”
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r8.anchor: ولما كانت الجنة الروحانية غير متراخية عن الموت في حق السعداء ، لا جرم قال : { فادخلى فى عبادى

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r14.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r14.claim: Entering among God's servants means joining the righteous, as in Solomon's supplication.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r14.anchor: Among My servants means among the righteous servants, as in the supplication of Solomon in 27:19

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r15.speaker: K
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r15.claim: The phrase is read as an address to the spiritual elect.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r15.anchor: In this sense it is read as an address to the spiritual elect

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r16.speaker: Q, R, Sy, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r16.claim: Others read the phrase as entering into the servants' bodies, referring to spirits returning to bodies in bodily resurrection; some allow both readings.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r16.anchor: Some read, “Enter into My servants,” meaning their bodies, thus alluding to spirits returning to bodies for the bodily resurrection

SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r1.claim: Fī ʿibādī may mean entering the bodies of God's servants or joining their company.
SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون: في جسد عبادي ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: في زمرة عبادي.

SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، جماعة
SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, and others read the singular ʿabdī, with the singular used generically.
SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعكرمة وجماعة " في عبدي " والمراد الجنس،

SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r3.claim: The first verb takes fī for figurative location, like entering a crowd, whereas the second takes a direct object for actual location; this explanation works if a believer's soul joins God's company.
SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r3.anchor: وتعدى الفعل الأول ب " في " لأن الظرف ليس بحقيقي نحو: " دخلت في غمار الناس " ،

SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r4.claim: If the soul is a spirit ordered into bodies, the locative relation is actual there as well.
SAMIN-DURR:89:29/r4.anchor: وأما إذا كان المراد بالنفس الروح، وأنها مأمورة بدخولها في الأجساد فالظرفية فيه متحققة أيضا.

TAB:89:27/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB:89:27/r8.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ places the call to return at death but says the command to enter among God's servants belongs to the Resurrection.
TAB:89:27/r8.anchor: عن أبي صالح ارْجِعي إلى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال :  هذا عند الموت فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال هذا يوم القيامة .

TAB:89:27/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r9.speaker: أبو أسامة بن زيد عن أبيه
TAB:89:27/r9.claim: A report says the tranquil soul is promised the Garden at death, on the Day of Gathering, and at resurrection.
TAB:89:27/r9.anchor: عن أُسامة بن زيد ،   عن أبيه ،   في قوله :  يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ قال :  بُشّرت بالجنة

TAB:89:29/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:29/r1.claim: One view says the angels call the believer's soul at resurrection to return to its body; Ibn ʿAbbās says tranquil souls return to bodies on that day.
TAB:89:29/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قوله :  يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ ارْجِعي إلى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال :  تردّ الأرواح

TAB:89:29/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:89:29/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God orders souls to return to bodies at resurrection, when they come to Him as He first created them.
TAB:89:29/r2.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  فادْخُلِي فِي عبادِي وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي يأمر الله الأرواح يوم القيامة أن ترجع إلى الأجساد

TAB:89:29/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB:89:29/r4.claim: Another view places the call to return at death, while the entry among God's servants is at resurrection.
TAB:89:29/r4.anchor: عن أبي صالح ارْجِعي إلَى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال :  هذا عند الموت فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال :  هذا يوم القيامة .

TAB:89:29/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r5.speaker: author
TAB:89:29/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the resurrection interpretation because the following words tell the soul to enter among God's servants and into His Garden.
TAB:89:29/r5.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب القول الذي ذكرناه عن ابن عباس والضحاك ،   أن ذلك إنما يقال لهم

TAB:89:29/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:29/r6.claim: Qatāda interprets entry among God's servants as joining the righteous servants.
TAB:89:29/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال :  ادخلي في عبادي الصالحين وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي .

TAB:89:29/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r7.speaker: محمد بن مزاحم
TAB:89:29/r7.claim: Muḥammad ibn Muzāḥim says entering among God's servants means entering His obedience, and entering His Garden means entering His mercy.
TAB:89:29/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن مزاحم أخي الضحاك بن مُزاحم :  فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال :  في طاعتي وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي قال :  في رحمتي .

TAB:89:29/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r8.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة
TAB:89:29/r8.claim: Some Basran grammarians understand entering among God's servants as entering His party.
TAB:89:29/r8.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة يوجّه معنى قوله :  فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادي إلى :  فادخلي في حزبي .

TAB:89:29/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:29/r10.claim: A variant attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās reads the singular servant instead of plural servants; al-Kalbī says this refers to the spirit returning to its body.
TAB:89:29/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   أنه قرأها :  «فادْخُلِي فِي عَبْدِي » على التوحيد .

TAB:89:29/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r11.speaker: author
TAB:89:29/r11.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the plural servants reading because the authoritative readers agree on it.
TAB:89:29/r11.anchor: والصواب من القراءة في ذلك فادخُلي في عِبادي بمعنى :  فادخلي في عبادي الصالحين .   لإجماع الحجة من القراء عليه

TAB:89:30/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:30/r1.claim: One view says the angels call the believer's soul at resurrection to return to its body; Ibn ʿAbbās says tranquil souls return to bodies on that day.
TAB:89:30/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قوله :  يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ ارْجِعي إلى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال :  تردّ الأرواح

TAB:89:30/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:89:30/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God orders souls to return to bodies at resurrection, when they come to Him as He first created them.
TAB:89:30/r2.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  فادْخُلِي فِي عبادِي وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي يأمر الله الأرواح يوم القيامة أن ترجع إلى الأجساد

TAB:89:30/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB:89:30/r4.claim: Another view places the call to return at death, while the entry among God's servants is at resurrection.
TAB:89:30/r4.anchor: عن أبي صالح ارْجِعي إلَى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال :  هذا عند الموت فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال :  هذا يوم القيامة .

TAB:89:30/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r5.speaker: author
TAB:89:30/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the resurrection interpretation because the following words tell the soul to enter among God's servants and into His Garden.
TAB:89:30/r5.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب القول الذي ذكرناه عن ابن عباس والضحاك ،   أن ذلك إنما يقال لهم

TAB:89:30/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:30/r6.claim: Qatāda interprets entry among God's servants as joining the righteous servants.
TAB:89:30/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال :  ادخلي في عبادي الصالحين وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي .

TAB:89:30/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r7.speaker: محمد بن مزاحم
TAB:89:30/r7.claim: Muḥammad ibn Muzāḥim says entering among God's servants means entering His obedience, and entering His Garden means entering His mercy.
TAB:89:30/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن مزاحم أخي الضحاك بن مُزاحم :  فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال :  في طاعتي وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي قال :  في رحمتي .

TAB:89:30/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r8.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة
TAB:89:30/r8.claim: Some Basran grammarians understand entering among God's servants as entering His party.
TAB:89:30/r8.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة يوجّه معنى قوله :  فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادي إلى :  فادخلي في حزبي .

TAB:89:30/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:30/r10.claim: A variant attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās reads the singular servant instead of plural servants; al-Kalbī says this refers to the spirit returning to its body.
TAB:89:30/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   أنه قرأها :  «فادْخُلِي فِي عَبْدِي » على التوحيد .

TAB:89:30/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r11.speaker: author
TAB:89:30/r11.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the plural servants reading because the authoritative readers agree on it.
TAB:89:30/r11.anchor: والصواب من القراءة في ذلك فادخُلي في عِبادي بمعنى :  فادخلي في عبادي الصالحين .   لإجماع الحجة من القراء عليه

TAB-FULL:v24p395/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r7.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r7.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ places the return at death and entry among God's servants at the Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r7.anchor: عن أبي صالح، {ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية} [الفجر: 28] قال: هذا عند الموت {فادخلي في عبادي} [الفجر: 29] قال هذا يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r6.claim: Qatāda explains entry among God's servants as joining the righteous servants.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {فادخلي في عبادي} [الفجر: 29] قال: ادخلي في عبادي الصالحين

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r7.speaker: محمد بن مزاحم
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r7.claim: Muḥammad b. Muzāḥim interprets entry among God's servants as entry into God's obedience and His Garden as His mercy.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن مزاحم، أخي الضحاك بن مزاحم: {فادخلي في عبادي} [الفجر: 29] قال: في طاعتي {وادخلي جنتي} [الفجر: 30] قال: في رحمتي

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r8.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r8.claim: Some Basran grammarians take 'among My servants' to mean among My party.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r8.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة يوجه معنى قوله: {فادخلي في عبادي} [الفجر: 29] إلى: فادخلي في حزبي

TAB-FULL:v24p399/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to read 'among My servant' in the singular.
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، أنه قرأها: «فادخلي في عبدي» على التوحيد

TAB-FULL:v24p399/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r3.speaker: أبو الشيخ الهنائي
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r3.claim: Abū al-Shaykh al-Hunāʾī is also reported to read the singular form.
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r3.anchor: عن أبي الشيخ الهنائي: (فادخلي في عبدي)

TAB-FULL:v24p399/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r4.speaker: الكلبي
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī explains the singular reading as the spirit returning to the body.
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r4.anchor: وفي قول الكلبي: (فادخلي في عبدي وادخلي في جنتي) يعني: الروح ترجع في الجسد

TAB-FULL:v24p399/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the plural 'My servants' because the authoritative readers agree on that form, meaning the righteous servants.
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r5.anchor: والصواب من القراءة في ذلك {فادخلي في عبادي} [الفجر: 29] بمعنى: فادخلي في عبادي الصالحين؛ لإجماع الحجة من القراء عليه

TABATABAI:89:29-30/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:29-30/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:29-30/r1.claim: The tranquil soul is admitted among God’s servants because it has abandoned independence, accepted God’s truth, and submits its being, acts, and choices to Him; entry among the servants affirms complete servitude.
TABATABAI:89:29-30/r1.anchor: لما اطمأن إلى ربه انقطع عن دعوى الاستقلال ورضي بما هو الحق من ربه

ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r5.claim: Fadkhulī fī ʿibādī means entering among God's chosen servants.

ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r6.claim: A reading has fī ʿabdī in the singular; on it, God may mean entering into the companion from whom the soul emerged.
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r6.anchor:
وقرئت فادخلي في عبدي.
(وادخلي جنتي (30)
فعلى هذه القراءة - والله أعلم - ادخلي إلى صاحبك الذي خرجت

ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r7.claim: The majority reading and interpretation are fī ʿibādī followed by wadkhulī jannatī.
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r7.anchor: والأكثر في القراءة والتفسير: (فادخلي في عبادي (29) وادخلي جنتي (30).

TABRISI:89:25/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:25/r15.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، الضحاك، ابن السميفع
TABRISI:89:25/r15.claim: These authorities have a variant reading fādخulī fī ʿabdī, with the singular “My servant.”
TABRISI:89:25/r15.anchor: وقرءة ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك وابن السميفع فادخلي في عبدي

TABRISI:89:29/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:29/r10.claim: Fī ʿabdī uses a singular form with a plural sense: God's servants are treated as one because they agree in worship.
TABRISI:89:29/r10.anchor: وقوله { في عبدي } لفظه لفظ الواحد ومعناه الجمع أي عبادي

TABRISI:89:29/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:89:29/r11.claim: A Prophetic saying likens the servants' unanimity to one hand united against outsiders.

TABRISI:89:29/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:29/r12.claim: Another interpretation takes “enter among My servant” as the soul returning to its servant's body.
TABRISI:89:29/r12.anchor: وقال غيره: معناه فادخلي في جسم عبدي

TABRISI:89:29-30/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29-30/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:29-30/r14.claim: Entering among God's servants means joining the chosen righteous; the possessive form honors them.
TABRISI:89:29-30/r14.anchor: أي في زمرة عبادي الصالحين المصطفين الذين رضيت عنهم وهذه نسبة تشريف وتعظيم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p529/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p529/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p529/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas’s singular reading “enter among My servant” is cited in support of the return-to-the-body interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p529/r6.anchor: يدل على هذا ما روي عن ابن عباس أنه قرأ:

WAHIDI-QT:89:29/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:89:29/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:89:29/r1.claim: At the Resurrection it is told to join the company of God's righteous servants.
WAHIDI-QT:89:29/r1.anchor: فاذا كان يوم القيامة قيل { فادخلي في عبادي } أي في جملة عبادي الصالحين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r4.claim: She is invited to join the company of God's righteous servants.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r4.anchor: فادخلي في عبادي } أي: في جملة عبادي الصالحين.

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r3.claim: Entering God’s servants means joining the sincere, distinguished, righteous servants devoted to Him.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r3.anchor: Bana ihlâs ile kulluk eden, Bana ihtisas ile temayüz eyleyen hâlis ibâd-ı sâlihîn zümresine katıl

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r5.claim: Another interpretation understands the entry as the soul entering bodies and then entering the abode of reward with them.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r5.anchor: Cesetlere gir, onlarla birlikte dâr-ı sevâba gir

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.claim: Exegetes differ on whether this address comes at death, resurrection, or after the reckoning; the author considers the last timing most apparent from the context.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.anchor: Bunda üç kavil vardır: Ölüm zamanında olması, ba‘s zamanında

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r19.claim: The fā in “enter among My servants” is explanatory, clarifying what returning means.

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r2.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r2.claim: On the resurrection reading, commentators who understand nafs as spirit interpret entering among the servants as the spirit returning to its separated body, a report also attributed to Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jubayr.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r2.anchor: bunun İbn Abbas’tan ve İbn Cübeyr’den mervî olduğunu da söylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r8.claim: On the death reading, the fā may indicate immediate joining of the near spirits in the spirit-world or joining the righteous after resurrection.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r8.anchor: bilâ terahî âlem-i ervâhta mukarrebîn silkine duhûl veya sonra ba‘s ile sâlihîn zümresine duhûl

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r9.speaker: Ebû Sâlih
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r9.claim: Abu Salih says returning to the Lord is at death as departure from the world, while entering among the servants and entering Paradise are commands at resurrection.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r9.anchor: Bu âyette ٱرْجِعِىٓ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ inde’l-mevttir

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.claim: Though Abu Salih’s reading seems apparent, the context favors the address after resurrection and completed reckoning; the reports can fit by treating each death as a person’s resurrection or the commands together as a unit.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.anchor: bu hitâbın da o güne ait olması iktizâ edeceğinden ba‘de’l-ba‘s

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.claim: The majority understand an omitted “God will say” from the preceding context, making the address and commands declarative and creative rather than legislative.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.anchor: cumhûrun muhtârı budur. Buna göre bu hitâbın ve emirlerin teşrî‘î değil tekvînî olması

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.claim: The author also considers a direct, legislative divine address at the surah’s conclusion plausible; separation from what precedes highlights that the tranquil souls themselves should hear it.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.anchor: bunun nüfûs-i mutmainne tarafından re’sen ve bilhassa istimâ‘ı maksud olduğuna tenbih için

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r17.claim: The causative fā commands worldly effort to increase righteous deeds, join God’s sincere servants free of Satan’s dominion, and belong to their group in this life and the next.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r17.anchor: dünyada rızâullâha muvâfık a‘mâl-i sâlihayı çoğaltarak üzerlerinde Şeytan’ın sultası olmayan

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.claim: The life of a tranquil soul among the righteous is like the ten nights before Eid al-Adha, and its entry into Paradise is the dawn of the greatest festival of bliss.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.anchor: dünya ömrü îd-i adhâya tekaddüm eden bir leyâl-i aşr

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.claim: The commentator prays that he and his readers return to God content and accepted, join His sincere servants, and reach Paradise and the vision of God.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.anchor: bu abd-i hakīri ve bunları hüsn-i nazarla okuyup ona hayırhah olanları

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r1.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r1.claim: Neuwirth rejects the Kufan division between the verses because the two related imperatives should not be separated.

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r2.claim: The author counters that ʿibādī and jannatī form an approximate rhyme if nonclassical vowel and consonant variations are allowed, as in other Quranic pairs.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Dagegen steht allerdings der zumindest näherungsweise Reimcharakter von ʿibādi / ǧannati

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r3.claim: For ʿabd, the note refers to 53:10.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Zum Ausdruck ʿabd vgl. die Anmerkung zu 53:10.

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r1.claim: Later verses 27–30 add a positive afterlife ending to the earlier threat-only conclusion, pairing entry into the Garden with the Hell mentioned in verse 23.

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.claim: All three insertions use direct speech: the human responds to worldly allotment and threatened Hell, then God's address to the trusting soul and servants supersedes those negative statements.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.anchor: Auffällig ist, dass alle drei Einschübe – V. 15.16, V. 23.24 und V. 27–30 – wörtliche Reden enthalten

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.claim: Addressing the person directly without an introductory afterlife formula is a graceful, warm honor that lets the promise of otherworldly happiness reach into this life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.anchor: doğrudan insana hitap edilmesi, Cenâb-ı Hakk’ın bu yapıdaki kullarına çok güzel bir iltifatı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r6.claim: God's calling the admitted to Paradise “My servants” is a supreme honor; their final gift is divine pleasure, greater than all other blessings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r6.anchor: “Benim kullarım” diye anması iltifatların en güzelidir

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p360/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p360/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك وأبو شيخ الهنائي والكلبي وابن السميفع
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p360/r2.claim: These readers use singular عبدي where the ordinary reading has plural عبادي; Ibn Jinnī says singular form conveys the community’s shared, undivided servitude.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p360/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك وأبي شيخ الهنائي والكلبي وابن السميفع:

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p360/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p360/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p360/r3.claim: He explains the collective singular as concord: believers stand together as one, like the Prophetic description that they are one hand against outsiders; he contrasts divided hearts.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p360/r3.anchor: وذلك أنه جعل عباده كالواحد، أي: لا خلاف بينهم في عبوديته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p131/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131/r1.claim: The soul is told to join the company of God's righteous, sincere servants and become one of their ranks.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131/r1.anchor: في زمرة عبادي الصالحين المخلصين لي وانتظمي في سلكهم وكوني في جملتهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r8.claim: Abu Salih says ‘return to your Lord’ is spoken when the soul leaves worldly life, while ‘enter among my servants and enter my Paradise’ is spoken at resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو صالح في قوله: "ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية" قال: هذا عند خروجها من الدنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p424#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p424#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p424#2/r1.claim: Entering among God’s servants means joining them in Paradise; another view specifies the obedient, chosen, righteous servants, as in the prayer to be admitted among the righteous.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p424#2/r1.anchor: أي مع عبادي في جنتي. وقيل: في جملة عبادي الصالحين المطيعين المصطفين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r2.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr recounts Ibn Abbas’s funeral: a strange bird entered the bier and never emerged, and the full ‘tranquil soul’ verses were recited at the grave by an unknown voice.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف فشهدت جنازته، فجاء طائر لم [نر] (1)

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r3.claim: Entering among God's servants means joining the righteous, or joining the near ones whose reciprocal illumination is like facing mirrors; it may also mean re-entering the bodies left behind.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r3.anchor: في جملة عبادي الصالحين. { وادخلي جنتي } معهم أو في زمرة المقربين فتستضيء بنورهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r5.claim: A report promises forgiveness for reciting al-Fajr during the ten nights and a light on the Resurrection Day for reciting it at other times.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r5.anchor: من قرأ سورة الفجر في الليالي العشر غفر له

BINTSHATI:v2p163/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r3.claim: Some interpret God's servants as His righteous servants.

BINTSHATI:v2p163/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r4.claim: Others interpret entering among God's servants as entering His obedience.

BINTSHATI:v2p163/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r5.claim: A further interpretation is to enter God's party or faction.

BINTSHATI:v2p163/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r6.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r6.claim: Al-Tabari selects the meaning 'enter among My righteous servants.'
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r6.anchor: واختار الإمام الطبري أن تكون بمعنى: فادخلي في عبادي الصالحين.

BINTSHATI:v2p163/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r7.claim: The author says the context needs no added adjective righteous: a tranquil soul promised Paradise must already be among God's righteous servants.
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r7.anchor: والمقام مستغنٍ عن وصفهم بالصالحين، إذ لا تكون النفس المطمئنة الموعودة بدخول الجنة، إلا من عباد الله الصالحين،

BINTSHATI:v2p163/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r8.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r8.claim: The concise use of servants parallels the promises in al-Zumar and al-Zukhruf.
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r8.anchor: ونظيره في القرآن الكريم آيتا الزمر 17:

BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r8.claim: Entering among God's servants means joining the company of the righteous who come to Him; a singular reading can also indicate return to servants' bodies.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r9.claim: The singular reading ʿabdī is taken as a generic singular encompassing few or many and supporting the interpretation of return to bodies.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r9.anchor: بالتوحيد للجنس الشامل للقليل والكثير تدل على ذلك

DURR-FULL:v8p513/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r6.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says God invited people to buy the well of Rūma, which ʿUthmān bought and made available for public drinking; the verses were then revealed about him.
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: من يشتري بئر رومة نستعذب بها غفر الله له

DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r6.speaker: أبي
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r6.claim: Ubayy’s reading adds “secure” before “tranquil” and reads the entry clause in the singular.
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي الشيخ الهنائي رضي الله عنه قال: في قراءة أبي يا أيتها النفس الآمنة المطمئنة فادخلي في عبدي

DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also recited the entry clause in the singular: “enter among My servant.”
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قرأها فادخلي في عبدي على التوحيد

DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the soul is pleased with its reward, God approves its deeds, and it enters among the believers.
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ارجعي إلى ربك راضية} قال: بما أعطيت من الثواب {مرضية} عنها بعملها

DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan says when God takes a believer’s soul, it rests in God and both are pleased; it is admitted to Paradise among the righteous.
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r11.anchor: في قوله: {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} الآية قال: إن الله إذا أراد قبض عبده المؤمن

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r1.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r1.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says return to God occurs at death as the soul leaves the world; at resurrection it is told to enter among God’s servants and into Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r1.anchor: قوله: {ارجعي إلى ربك} قال: هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r5.claim: Qatāda identifies it as the believer who trusts God’s promise; entering among God’s servants means entering the righteous and Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r5.anchor: عن قتادة {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} قال: هذا المؤمن اطمأن إلى ما وعد الله

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r8.claim: Al-Suddī glosses “enter among My servants” as joining them.

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the believer receives glad tidings of Paradise at death, resurrection, and the gathering.
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r9.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم رضي الله عنه {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} الآية قال: بشرت بالجنة عند الموت وعند البعث ويوم الجمع

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r10.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr recounts a mysterious bird entering Ibn ʿAbbās’s coffin and never being seen again; the tranquil-soul verses were recited at his grave by an unknown person.
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال: مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف فجاء طير لم تر عين خلقته فدخل نعشه

TAB:89:28/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:28/r6.claim: Qatada interprets entering among God’s servants as joining the righteous servants.
TAB:89:28/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله : فادْخُلِي فِي عِبَادِي قال : ادخلي في عبادي الصالحين وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي

TAB:89:28/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r7.speaker: محمد بن مزاحم
TAB:89:28/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Muzahim takes God’s servants as His obedience and God’s garden as His mercy.
TAB:89:28/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن مزاحم أخي الضحاك بن مزاحم : فادخلي في عبادي قال : في طاعتي

TAB:89:28/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r8.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة
TAB:89:28/r8.claim: Some Basran grammarians understand God’s servants as His party.
TAB:89:28/r8.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة يوجه معنى قوله : فادخلي في عبادي إلى : فادخلي في حزبي

TAB:89:28/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:28/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to have read the phrase in the singular, fi ʿabdi, instead of the canonical plural.
TAB:89:28/r11.anchor: عن سليمان بن قَتّةَ ، عن ابن عباس ، أنه قرأها

TAB:89:28/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r12.speaker: أبو الشيخ الهنائي
TAB:89:28/r12.claim: Abu al-Shaykh al-Hunaʾi is also reported to read the singular fi ʿabdi.
TAB:89:28/r12.anchor: ثني هلال ، عن أبي الشيخ الهنائي

TAB:89:28/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r13.speaker: الكلبي
TAB:89:28/r13.claim: Al-Kalbi’s singular reading means that the soul returns into the body.
TAB:89:28/r13.anchor: وفي قول الكلبيّ : «فادْخُلِي فِي عَبْدِي ، وَادْخُلِي فِي جَنّتِي »

TAB:89:28/r14.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r14.speaker: author
TAB:89:28/r14.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the agreed plural reading, meaning that the soul enters among God’s righteous servants.
TAB:89:28/r14.anchor: والصواب من القراءة في ذلك فادخُلي في عِبادي بمعنى : فادخلي في عبادي الصالحين

BURHAN:v4p302/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p302/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p302/r1.claim: في has spatial containment senses: both place and contained thing may be physical or conceptual, or one physical and one abstract; the first is literal and the fourth metaphor is closest to literal.
BURHAN:v4p302/r1.anchor: للظرفية ثم تارة يكون الظرف والمظروف حسيين نحو زيد في الدار

BURHAN:v4p302/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p302/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p302/r2.claim: في can mean مع, “with,” in the command to enter among God's servants.
BURHAN:v4p302/r2.anchor: والرابع أقرب المجازات إلى الحقيقة وتجيء بمعنى مع

ABUHAYYAN:89:29/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:29/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:29/r1.claim: The soul is told to enter among the company of God’s righteous servants.
ABUHAYYAN:89:29/r1.anchor: { فادخلي في عبادي } : أي في جملة عبادي الصالحين .

ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r2.claim: Another view takes the soul as spirit and reads the phrase as entering the bodies of God’s servants.
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r2.anchor: وقيل : النفس والروح ، والمعنى : فادخلي في أجساد عبادي .

ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r3.speaker: الجمهور وابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد وأبو جعفر وأبو صالح والكلبي وأبو شيخ الهنائي واليماني
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r3.claim: The majority read the plural ʿibādī; the named group reads the singular ʿabdī, which most likely is generic and has the same referent as the plural.
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { في عبادي } جمعاً ؛ وابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد وأبو جعفر وأبو صالح والكلبي وأبو شيخ الهنائي واليماني : في عبدي على الإفراد

ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r4.claim: The author prefers the generic-singular reading as equivalent in reference to the plural.
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r4.anchor: والأظهر أنه أريد به اسم الجنس ، فمدلوله ومدلول الجمع واحد .

ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r5.claim: Another explanation takes the singular as direct address to the soul and means entering the servant’s body.
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r5.anchor: وقيل : هو على حذف خاطب النفس مفردة فقال : فادخلي في عبدي : أي في جسد عبدي .

ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r6.claim: Entering a nonliteral domain takes fī, while a literal container usually follows the verb directly, explaining the different constructions.
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r6.anchor: وتعدى فادخلي أولاً بفي ، وثانياً بغير فاء ، وذلك أنه إذا كان المدخول فيه غير ظرف حقيقي تعددت إليه بفي

ALUSI:89:29/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r1.claim: Entering among God’s servants means joining the company and ranks of His sincere, righteous servants.
ALUSI:89:29/r1.anchor: في زمرة عبادي الصالحين المخلصين لي وانتظمي في سلكهم وكوني في جملتهم

ALUSI:89:29/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r3.claim: The first command signifies spiritual happiness through companionship with the righteous; the second signifies bodily happiness, and the superior spiritual reward is mentioned first, with the Garden completing it.
ALUSI:89:29/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى السعادة الروحانية لكمال استئناس النفس بالجليس الصالح والأمر بدخول الجنة إشارة إلى السعادة الجسمانية

ALUSI:89:29/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:89:29/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan explains that dukhūl takes fī with a figurative or nonliteral domain, but usually takes a real container directly.
ALUSI:89:29/r4.anchor: قال أبو حيان لأن المدخول فيه إن كان غير ظرف حقيقي تعدى إليه في الاستعمال بفي

ALUSI:89:29/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r5.claim: One reading takes ‘return to your Lord’s promise’ as the promised Garden and company of the righteous, spoken after the reckoning; the objection that this implies prior residence is answered by a potential existence in Adam’s loins while he was in the Garden.
ALUSI:89:29/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى موعد ربك واستظهر أن المراد بموعده تعالى

ALUSI:89:29/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r6.claim: The proposed prior existence is compared with reports from ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās that maʿād in 28:85 means Paradise rather than Mecca; this works only if Adam’s Garden was the eschatological Garden, a strongly disputed identification discussed by Ibn al-Qayyim.
ALUSI:89:29/r6.anchor: على ما روى عن أمير المؤمنين علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما من أن المراد بالمعاد الجنة دون مكة

ALUSI:89:29/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r7.claim: Another interpretation makes ‘return to your Lord’s command’ mean return to one of His affairs: His treatment of her without distress, placement in an honored station, or something similar.
ALUSI:89:29/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى أمر ربك واستظهر أن المراد بالأمر على ذلك التقدير

ALUSI:89:29/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r8.claim: A further view understands the return as return to God’s general favor, from the barzakh after death or from the period after resurrection but before judgment.
ALUSI:89:29/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى كرامة ربك ويراد جنس كرامته سبحانه

ALUSI:89:29/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r9.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
ALUSI:89:29/r9.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk place the address at resurrection; on one analysis nafs means the person, Lord means God, and an implied noun supplies the station to which she returns.
ALUSI:89:29/r9.anchor: وعن عكرمة والضحاك أن ذلك القول عند البعث فقيل النفس بمعنى الذات أيضاً والمراد بالرب هو الله عز وجل

ALUSI:89:29/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r10.claim: Another analysis takes nafs as the soul and rabb as its owner, the body: the soul returns to its former body, then enters the servants and the abode of reward.
ALUSI:89:29/r10.anchor: وقيل النفس بمعنى الروح والمراد بالرب الصاحب وفسر بالجسد وباقي الآية على حاله

ALUSI:89:29/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير
ALUSI:89:29/r11.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Jubayr reads ‘among My servants’ elliptically as ‘among the bodies of My servants’; singular first and plural second are compatible because the plural is generic.
ALUSI:89:29/r11.anchor: وجاء هذا في رواية عن ابن عباس وابن جبير ولا يضر الأفراد أولاً والجمع ثانياً

ALUSI:89:29/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r12.speaker: ابن زيد وجماعة
ALUSI:89:29/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd and a group say the address comes at death, with the soul understood as the spirit returning to the sacred realm and then joining the close servants.
ALUSI:89:29/r12.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وجماعة إن ذلك القول عند الموت

ALUSI:89:29/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r15.claim: On the death-time reading, the soul is pleased with its bliss and pleasing to God; entry among the close servants follows immediately, while entry into the eternal Garden follows at resurrection, though certainty permits the future event to follow by fa.
ALUSI:89:29/r15.anchor: وهذا الدخولان يعقبان الرجوع إلا أن الدخول الأول يعقبه بلا تراخ قبل يوم القيامة والثاني يعقبه بتراخ

ALUSI:89:29/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r16.claim: Other proposed sequencing allows both commands without delay: entry among the servants may mean joining righteous souls of one’s kind or their bodies, and Garden entry may be temporary enjoyment before the Hour.
ALUSI:89:29/r16.anchor: وجوز أن يكون تعقيب الأمرين بلا تراخ إن أريد بالدخول في العباد الدخول في زمرة المقربين

ALUSI:89:29/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r17.claim: The temporary-Garden proposal cites a hadith that believers’ souls are in birds’ crops in Paradise and an athar that a believer receives half his promised Garden at death; al-Ālūsī calls the mirror-and-radiance explanation of their gathering rhetorical speculation.
ALUSI:89:29/r17.anchor: ففي الحديث أن أرواح المؤمنين في حواصل طيور في الجنة وفي بعض الآثار إذا مات المؤمن أعطى نصف الجنة

ALUSI:89:29/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r18.speaker: أبو صالح
ALUSI:89:29/r18.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says the return is at death, meaning departure from worldly life, while the two entry commands are spoken at resurrection.
ALUSI:89:29/r18.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن أبي صالح أنه قال في الآية

ALUSI:89:29/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r19.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
ALUSI:89:29/r19.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī places the address after death but before resurrection: the believer sees his Garden home, returns to the body, and awaits questioning by Munkar and Nakīr; no grading is stated.
ALUSI:89:29/r19.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن محمد بن كعب القرظي أنه قال في الآية إن المؤمن إذا مات

ALUSI:89:29/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r21.claim: An inward reading applies the commands throughout earthly life: turn to God in every matter, join the sincere servants through good works, and enter the Garden potentially; al-Ālūsī says this is not a sound interpretation.
ALUSI:89:29/r21.anchor: وقيل يجوز أن يكون ذلك في سائر أوقات النفس في حياتها الدنيا

ALUSI:89:29/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r26.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد وأبو جعفر وأبو صالح وأبو شيخ واليماني
ALUSI:89:29/r26.claim: These authorities read ʿibādī in the singular, ʿabdī; al-Ālūsī takes the intended sense to be generic, as with nafs.
ALUSI:89:29/r26.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد وأبو جعفر وأبو صالح وأبو شيخ واليماني في عبدي على الأفراد

ALUSI:89:30/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r1.claim: Entering among God’s servants means joining the company and ranks of His sincere, righteous servants.
ALUSI:89:30/r1.anchor: في زمرة عبادي الصالحين المخلصين لي وانتظمي في سلكهم وكوني في جملتهم

ALUSI:89:30/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r3.claim: The first command signifies spiritual happiness through companionship with the righteous; the second signifies bodily happiness, and the superior spiritual reward is mentioned first, with the Garden completing it.
ALUSI:89:30/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى السعادة الروحانية لكمال استئناس النفس بالجليس الصالح والأمر بدخول الجنة إشارة إلى السعادة الجسمانية

ALUSI:89:30/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:89:30/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan explains that dukhūl takes fī with a figurative or nonliteral domain, but usually takes a real container directly.
ALUSI:89:30/r4.anchor: قال أبو حيان لأن المدخول فيه إن كان غير ظرف حقيقي تعدى إليه في الاستعمال بفي

ALUSI:89:30/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r5.claim: One reading takes ‘return to your Lord’s promise’ as the promised Garden and company of the righteous, spoken after the reckoning; the objection that this implies prior residence is answered by a potential existence in Adam’s loins while he was in the Garden.
ALUSI:89:30/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى موعد ربك واستظهر أن المراد بموعده تعالى

ALUSI:89:30/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r6.claim: The proposed prior existence is compared with reports from ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās that maʿād in 28:85 means Paradise rather than Mecca; this works only if Adam’s Garden was the eschatological Garden, a strongly disputed identification discussed by Ibn al-Qayyim.
ALUSI:89:30/r6.anchor: على ما روى عن أمير المؤمنين علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما من أن المراد بالمعاد الجنة دون مكة

ALUSI:89:30/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r7.claim: Another interpretation makes ‘return to your Lord’s command’ mean return to one of His affairs: His treatment of her without distress, placement in an honored station, or something similar.
ALUSI:89:30/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى أمر ربك واستظهر أن المراد بالأمر على ذلك التقدير

ALUSI:89:30/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r8.claim: A further view understands the return as return to God’s general favor, from the barzakh after death or from the period after resurrection but before judgment.
ALUSI:89:30/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى كرامة ربك ويراد جنس كرامته سبحانه

ALUSI:89:30/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r9.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
ALUSI:89:30/r9.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk place the address at resurrection; on one analysis nafs means the person, Lord means God, and an implied noun supplies the station to which she returns.
ALUSI:89:30/r9.anchor: وعن عكرمة والضحاك أن ذلك القول عند البعث فقيل النفس بمعنى الذات أيضاً والمراد بالرب هو الله عز وجل

ALUSI:89:30/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r10.claim: Another analysis takes nafs as the soul and rabb as its owner, the body: the soul returns to its former body, then enters the servants and the abode of reward.
ALUSI:89:30/r10.anchor: وقيل النفس بمعنى الروح والمراد بالرب الصاحب وفسر بالجسد وباقي الآية على حاله

ALUSI:89:30/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير
ALUSI:89:30/r11.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Jubayr reads ‘among My servants’ elliptically as ‘among the bodies of My servants’; singular first and plural second are compatible because the plural is generic.
ALUSI:89:30/r11.anchor: وجاء هذا في رواية عن ابن عباس وابن جبير ولا يضر الأفراد أولاً والجمع ثانياً

ALUSI:89:30/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r12.speaker: ابن زيد وجماعة
ALUSI:89:30/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd and a group say the address comes at death, with the soul understood as the spirit returning to the sacred realm and then joining the close servants.
ALUSI:89:30/r12.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وجماعة إن ذلك القول عند الموت

ALUSI:89:30/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r15.claim: On the death-time reading, the soul is pleased with its bliss and pleasing to God; entry among the close servants follows immediately, while entry into the eternal Garden follows at resurrection, though certainty permits the future event to follow by fa.
ALUSI:89:30/r15.anchor: وهذا الدخولان يعقبان الرجوع إلا أن الدخول الأول يعقبه بلا تراخ قبل يوم القيامة والثاني يعقبه بتراخ

ALUSI:89:30/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r16.claim: Other proposed sequencing allows both commands without delay: entry among the servants may mean joining righteous souls of one’s kind or their bodies, and Garden entry may be temporary enjoyment before the Hour.
ALUSI:89:30/r16.anchor: وجوز أن يكون تعقيب الأمرين بلا تراخ إن أريد بالدخول في العباد الدخول في زمرة المقربين

ALUSI:89:30/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r17.claim: The temporary-Garden proposal cites a hadith that believers’ souls are in birds’ crops in Paradise and an athar that a believer receives half his promised Garden at death; al-Ālūsī calls the mirror-and-radiance explanation of their gathering rhetorical speculation.

BAGHAWI:89:29/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:29/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:89:29/r1.claim: Enter among My servants means enter Paradise together with God's servants; another explanation is to join His righteous, obedient, chosen servants, as in the prayer of Solomon.
BAGHAWI:89:29/r1.anchor: يعني مع عبادي في جنتي .   وقيل : في جملة عبادي الصالحين المطيعين المصطفين

BAGHAWI:89:30/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:30/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI:89:30/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that at Ibn Abbas's funeral in Taif a strange bird entered his bier and was not seen leaving; these verses were recited at his grave, though the reciter was unknown.
BAGHAWI:89:30/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : مات ابن عباس بالطائف فشهدت جنازته ،   فجاء طائر لم ير على صورة خلقه فدخل نعشه

BAYDAWI:89:29/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:29/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:29/r1.claim: The soul is told to enter the company of God's righteous servants.

BIQAI:89:29/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:29/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:29/r1.claim: Entering among God's servants means joining the company of the righteous who come to Him and are worthy of being attributed to Him.
BIQAI:89:29/r1.anchor: أي في زمرة الصالحين الوافدين عليَّ

BIQAI:89:29/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:29/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:29/r2.claim: Alternatively, it can mean entering the bodies of God's servants, the bodies the souls left in earthly life.
BIQAI:89:29/r2.anchor: أو في أجساد عبادي التي خرجت في الدنيا منها

BIQAI:89:29/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:29/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:29/r3.claim: The singular reading “عبدي” can be generic and include few or many, supporting the interpretation that the soul returns to its former body.
BIQAI:89:29/r3.anchor: بالتوحيد للجنس الشامل للقليل والكثير تدل على ذلك

DURR:89:28/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:28/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the soul is pleased with the reward given, approved because of its deeds, and told to enter among the believing servants.
DURR:89:28/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك راضية }

DURR:89:28/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR:89:28/r4.claim: Hasan says at a believer's death the soul finds rest in God, is pleased with Him and He with it; God takes it, admits it to Paradise, and makes it one of His righteous servants.
DURR:89:28/r4.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة } الآية ، قال : إن الله إذا أراد قبض عبده المؤمن اطمأنت النفس إليه

DURR:89:28/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR:89:28/r5.claim: Abu Salih locates the soul's return to God at death as it leaves the world; the commands to join God's servants and enter Paradise come on the Day of Resurrection.
DURR:89:28/r5.anchor: عن أبي صالح رضي الله عنه في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا

DURR:89:28/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR:89:28/r9.claim: Qatada says the believer is reassured by God's promise; entering among God's servants means joining the righteous, followed by entry into Paradise.
DURR:89:28/r9.anchor: عن قتادة { يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة } قال : هذا المؤمن اطمأن إلى ما وعد الله { فادخلي في عبادي } قال : ادخلي في الصالحين

DURR:89:28/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r12.speaker: السدي
DURR:89:28/r12.claim: Al-Suddi glosses 'among My servants' as 'with My servants.'
DURR:89:28/r12.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه { فادخلي في عبادي } قال : مع عبادي

DURR:89:28/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:89:28/r14.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr recounts that an unfamiliar bird entered Ibn Abbas's bier and was never seen leaving; as Ibn Abbas was buried, this passage was recited at the grave edge by an unknown speaker.
DURR:89:28/r14.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال : مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف

DURR:89:29/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:29/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:29/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the soul is content with the reward it received, approved because of its deeds, and enters among the believers.
DURR:89:29/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك راضية } قال : بما أعطيت من الثواب

DURR:89:29/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:29/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR:89:29/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says that when God takes a believer, the soul and God are mutually at ease and satisfied; God then admits it to Paradise among the righteous.
DURR:89:29/r4.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة } الآية ، قال : إن الله إذا أراد قبض عبده المؤمن

DURR:89:29/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:29/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR:89:29/r5.claim: Abu Salih distinguishes the soul's return at death, as it leaves worldly life, from the command at Resurrection to enter God's servants and Paradise.
DURR:89:29/r5.anchor: عن أبي صالح رضي الله عنه في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا
