DURR:89:29/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR:89:29/r9.claim: Qatada identifies the tranquil soul as the believer assured by God's promise, and explains entering among God's servants as joining the righteous.
DURR:89:29/r9.anchor: عن قتادة { يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة } قال : هذا المؤمن اطمأن إلى ما وعد الله { فادخلي في عبادي } قال : ادخلي في الصالحين

IBNASHUR:89:28/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r8.claim: The possessive forms ‘My servants’ and ‘My Garden’ shift from third-person reference to first-person speech.

IBNASHUR:89:29/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:29/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:29/r1.claim: The two commands spell out the preceding general good news; this detail after summary renews the recipients' joy.
IBNASHUR:89:29/r1.anchor: فهو تفصيل بعد الإجمال لتكرير إدخال السرور

IBNASHUR:89:29/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:29/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:29/r2.claim: ‘Among My servants’ means joining the company of the righteous, indicated by the possessive context and pairing with ‘My Garden’.
IBNASHUR:89:29/r2.anchor: والمعنى : ادخلي في زمرة عبادي . والمراد العباد الصالحون

IBNASHUR:89:29/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:29/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:29/r3.claim: This parallels the promise to admit believers among the righteous.
IBNASHUR:89:29/r3.anchor: ومعنى هذا كقوله تعالى : { لندخلنهم في الصالحين }

IBNASHUR:89:29/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:29/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:29/r4.claim: The preposition expresses real inclusion, which amounts to companionship with those blessed by God.
IBNASHUR:89:29/r4.anchor: فالظرفية حقيقية وتؤول إلى معنى المعية كقوله تعالى

IBNATIYYA:89:28/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r2.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r2.claim: The majority reading has the plural ʿibādī; the phrase means joining the ranks of God's righteous servants.
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى : ( في عبادي ) أي في عداد عبادي الصالحين وهذه قراءة الجمهور بجمع ( عبادي )

IBNATIYYA:89:28/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r4.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r4.claim: Some take rabb as the human body containing the soul: “return to your Lord” means enter the bodies, with nafs used generically; Ibn Abbas's singular reading and Ibn Masud's “in my servant's body” support this.
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r4.anchor: وقيل الرب هنا : الإنسان ذو النفس ، أي : ادخلي في الأجساد ، و ( النفس ) اسم جنس

IBNATIYYA:89:28/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r5.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r5.claim: Another view makes the address a present exhortation to believers, as a counterpart to the description of disbelievers: persist and strive until you return satisfied and approved; nafs is generic here too.
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r5.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء : هذا النداء هو الآن للمؤمنين كما ذكر الله تعالى حال الكافرين قال : يا مؤمنون

IBNATIYYA:89:29/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وأبو شيخ والضحاك واليماني ومجاهد وأبو جعفر
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r1.claim: These authorities read “so enter me among my servant,” which makes the soul a particular individual rather than a generic class.
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ، وعكرمة ، وأبو شيخ ، والضحاك ، واليماني ، ومجاهد ، وأبو جعفر فادخلني في عبدي ) ، فالنفس –على هذا- ليست باسم الجنس

IBNATIYYA:89:29/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r2.speaker: أبو شيخ
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r2.claim: Abu Shaykh says that on this reading the spirit enters the body.
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r2.anchor: قال أبو شيخ : الروح تدخل في البدن

IBNATIYYA:89:29/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b's codex has an expanded wording describing the secure, assured soul as pleased and approved, then telling it to return among God's servant.

IBNATIYYA:89:29/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r4.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r4.claim: Salim ibn Abd Allah reads “enter among My servants, and enter My garden.”
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r4.anchor: وقرأ سالم بن عبد الله : " فادخلي في عبادي ولجي جنتي "

IBNATIYYA:89:29/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r5.claim: The singular ʿabdī may function generically, portraying God's servants as one united body; Ibn Atiyya compares this to the saying that believers are one hand against others.
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r5.anchor: اسم جنس ، جعل عباده كالشيء الواحد دلالة على الالتحام

IBNATIYYA:89:29/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r6.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r6.claim: Others place the call at the gathering when those bound for Hell are led away; the souls are addressed together with their owners, “return” means to God's mercy, and the servants are the righteous and God-fearing.
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون : هذا النداء إنما هو الموقف عندما ينطلق بأهل النار إلى النار ، فنداء النفوس على هذا إنما هو نداء أرباب النفوس مع النفوس

IBNATIYYA:89:30/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r1.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r1.claim: Salim ibn Abd Allah reads “enter among My servants, and enter My garden.”
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r1.anchor: وقرأ سالم بن عبد الله : " فادخلي في عبادي ولجي جنتي "

IBNATIYYA:89:30/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وأبو شيخ والضحاك واليماني ومجاهد وأبو جعفر
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r2.claim: The cited variant reads “enter me among my servant”; the passage says this makes the soul a particular individual, and Abu Shaykh says the spirit enters the body.
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ، وعكرمة ، وأبو شيخ ، والضحاك ، واليماني ، ومجاهد ، وأبو جعفر فادخلني في عبدي ) ، فالنفس –على هذا- ليست باسم الجنس

IBNATIYYA:89:30/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r3.claim: Ubayy's codex expands the address to the assured soul and ends by telling it to return among God's servant.

IBNATIYYA:89:30/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r4.claim: The singular “My servant” may be generic, presenting all God's servants as one united body, like the saying that believers are one hand against others.
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r4.anchor: اسم جنس ، جعل عباده كالشيء الواحد دلالة على الالتحام

IBNATIYYA:89:30/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r5.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r5.claim: Others place the address at the gathering when people bound for Hell are led away; the souls are addressed with their owners, return is to God's mercy, and the servants are the righteous and God-fearing.
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون : هذا النداء إنما هو الموقف عندما ينطلق بأهل النار إلى النار ، فنداء النفوس على هذا إنما هو نداء أرباب النفوس مع النفوس

IBNKATHIR:89:27/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r4.claim: God calls the soul to join His servants and enter Paradise; this address comes at death and again on Resurrection, as angels announce the believer at death and rising from the grave.
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r4.anchor: وهذا يقال لها عند الاحتضار ، وفي يوم القيامة أيضا ، كما أن الملائكة يبشرون المؤمن عند احتضاره

IBNKATHIR:89:27/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r8.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to read “enter My servant” in the singular; ʿIkrima and al-Kalbī say likewise, and Ibn Jarīr chooses this reading, though Ibn Kathir calls it unusual.

IBNKATHIR:89:27/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir favors the apparent plural reading, linking return to God’s judgment and presence in 6:62 and 40:43.
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r9.anchor: والظاهر الأول ؛ لقوله : { ثُمَّ رُدُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ مَوْلَاهُمُ الْحَقِّ }

KASHSHAF:89:29/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:29/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:29/r1.claim: Enter among God's righteous servants and join their ranks.
KASHSHAF:89:29/r1.anchor: في جملة عبادي الصالحين ،   وانتظمي في سلكهم

MAWARDI:89:29/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:29/r1.speaker: أُبيّ بن كعب
MAWARDI:89:29/r1.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's reading has the singular, enter among My servant.
MAWARDI:89:29/r1.anchor: أحدها : في عبدي ،   وهو في حرف أُبيّ بن كعب

MAWARDI:89:29/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:29/r2.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:89:29/r2.claim: The phrase can mean enter into My obedience.

MAWARDI:89:29/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:29/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI:89:29/r3.claim: It can mean enter among My servants.
MAWARDI:89:29/r3.anchor: الثالث : معناه فادخلي{[3264]} مع عبادي ،   قاله السدي

NASAFI:89:29/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:29/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:29/r1.claim: Enter among God's righteous servants and join their company.
NASAFI:89:29/r1.anchor: { فادخلى فِى عِبَادِى } في جملة عبادي الصالحين فانتظمي في سلكهم

NASAFI:89:30/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:30/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
NASAFI:89:30/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda takes “among My servants” to mean with or among God's chosen servants.
NASAFI:89:30/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : أي مع عبادي أو بين عبادي أي خواصي كما قال

NASAFI:89:30/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:30/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:30/r3.claim: Another view takes the soul to mean the spirit, entering the bodies of God's servants.
NASAFI:89:30/r3.anchor: وقيل : النفس الروح ومعناه فادخلي في أجساد عبادي كقراءة عبد الله بن مسعود

NASAFI:89:30/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:30/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
NASAFI:89:30/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's reading has “in the body of My servant.”
NASAFI:89:30/r4.anchor: كقراءة عبد الله بن مسعود { فِي جسد عبدي } ولما مات ابن عباس بالطائف

QURTUBI:89:29/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:29/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:29/r1.claim: Enter among My servants means enter the bodies of My servants, supported by Ibn Abbas's and Ibn Masud's readings.
QURTUBI:89:29/r1.anchor: " فادخلي في عبادي " أي في أجساد عبادي ، دليله قراءة ابن عباس وابن مسعود

QURTUBI:89:29/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:29/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
QURTUBI:89:29/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak say this entry occurs on the Day of Resurrection.
QURTUBI:89:29/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هذا يوم القيامة ، وقاله الضحاك

QURTUBI:89:29/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:29/r3.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI:89:29/r3.claim: The majority describe Paradise as the eternal home and dwelling of the righteous and virtuous.
QURTUBI:89:29/r3.anchor: والجمهور على أن الجنة هي دار الخلود التي هي مسكن الأبرار ، ودار الصالحين والأخيار

QURTUBI:89:29/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:29/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:29/r4.claim: Among My servants means among the righteous, as in 29:9, which says God will admit them among the righteous.
QURTUBI:89:29/r4.anchor: ومعنى " في عبادي " أي في الصالحين من عبادي ، كما قال :

QURTUBI:89:29/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:29/r5.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI:89:29/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash interprets My servants as My party or company: join their ranks.
QURTUBI:89:29/r5.anchor: وقال الأخفش : " في عبادي " أي في حزبي ، والمعنى واحد . أي انتظمي في سلكهم

RAZI:89:27/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:27/r3.speaker: القفال
RAZI:89:27/r3.claim: Al-Qaffāl reads the imperative as a report in meaning: when the soul is tranquil, it returns to God and is told to enter among His servants and His garden.
RAZI:89:27/r3.anchor: وقال القفال : هذا وإن كان أمرا في الظاهر لكنه خبر في المعنى

RAZI:89:28/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:28/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:89:28/r3.claim: If the address occurs at resurrection, “return” means return to the Lord’s reward and reenter the body from which the soul departed.

RAZI:89:29/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:29/r1.speaker: قيل
RAZI:89:29/r1.claim: One reported occasion identifies the verse as revealed concerning Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
RAZI:89:29/r1.anchor: قيل : نزلت في حمزة بن عبد المطلب

RAZI:89:29/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:29/r2.speaker: قيل
RAZI:89:29/r2.claim: Another report concerns Khubayb ibn ʿAdī, crucified by Meccans; after he prayed for his face to turn toward God’s city, God turned it and no one could turn it back.
RAZI:89:29/r2.anchor: في خبيب بن عدي الذي صلبه أهل مكة

RAZI:89:29/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:29/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:89:29/r3.claim: Although specific occasions are reported, the lesson follows the wording’s generality rather than a particular cause.
RAZI:89:29/r3.anchor: أن العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب

RAZI:89:29/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:29/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:89:29/r4.claim: Entering among God’s servants means joining His servants brought near to Him, a noble state.
RAZI:89:29/r4.anchor: إلى عبادي المقربين ،   وهذه حالة شريفة

RAZI:89:29/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:29/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:89:29/r5.claim: Pure souls resemble polished mirrors; when joined, they reflect one another’s rays, increasing spiritual bliss and rank.
RAZI:89:29/r5.anchor: الأرواح الشريفة القدسية تكون كالمرايا المصقولة

RAZI:89:29/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:29/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:89:29/r6.claim: This joining and its spiritual happiness are illustrated by the greeting to those on the right.
RAZI:89:29/r6.anchor: من قوله تعالى : { وأما إن كان من أصحاب اليمين فسلام لك

RAZI:89:30/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:30/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:89:30/r2.claim: The spiritual garden is attained immediately after death, so it follows with fa; bodily Paradise comes only after the great Resurrection, so it follows with wa.
RAZI:89:30/r2.anchor: ولما كانت الجنة الروحانية غير متراخية عن الموت في حق السعداء
